metadata.title: The Fastest Travel Together: Chemical Tagging of the Fastest Stars in Gaia DR2 to the Stellar Halo

evidence.quote: Marchetti et al. (2018) then adopted a model Galactic potential (see their section 4.1 for details) and identified 28 extreme-velocity stars that they estimated to have a greater than 50% probability of being on unbound orbits.
We selected five candidate extreme-velocity stars, accessible from Apache Point Observatory (APO) in May 2018, from the sample of Marchetti et al. (2018).

The elemental abundances we reported above for five of the 28 HVS candidates from Marchetti et al. (2018) which those authors find to have high probability of being unbound to the Milky Way, indicate that these stars do not originate in either the Galactic thin disc or the LMC.

notes: All nine stars are included as follow_up, not candidates_found: the paper follows them because Marchetti et al. (2018) had estimated a parent set to have >50% probability of being unbound (T:p2-b7), but its final assessment is that 'these stars are most likely just bound halo stars that are at the tail of its velocity distribution' (T:p12-b9), so no star retains unbound candidacy. The five APO targets are the five full Gaia DR2 identifiers in T:p4-b0; the four survey targets are named in T:p3-b7. Per-star notes: Gaia DR2 1508756353921427328 — APO target (T:p3-b3; T:p4-b0); Gaia DR2 1364548016594914560 — APO target (T:p3-b3; T:p4-b0); Gaia DR2 4593398670455374592 — APO target (T:p3-b3; T:p4-b0); Gaia DR2 4248140165233284352 — APO target (T:p3-b3; T:p4-b0); Gaia DR2 2233912206910720000 — APO target (T:p3-b3; T:p4-b0); Gaia DR2 1268023196461923712 — survey target, counted once although found in both APOGEE and LAMOST (T:p3-b7; I:p4-b1); Gaia DR2 6639557580310606976 — RAVE target (T:p3-b7; I:p4-b1); Gaia DR2 5212817273334550016 — RAVE target (T:p3-b7; I:p4-b1); Gaia DR2 4916199478888664320 — RAVE target (T:p3-b7; I:p4-b1). The HD 122563 and HD 84937 rows are radial-velocity standards, not unbound-candidate follow-up (T:p3-b3; I:p3-b1), and are excluded.

Gaia DR2 1508756353921427328: Table 1 gives P_MW = 0.99 for this star, but the paper defines P_MW as the probability of originating in the Milky Way disc, not as a bound probability; therefore it is not recorded as bound_probability. No distance, parallax, or proper-motion values for this target are reported in the supplied material. See T:p3-b0 and T:p3-b1.

Gaia DR2 1364548016594914560: For Gaia DR2 1364548016594914560, Table 1 reports the Gaia RV uncertainty as ±44 km s−1; this unusually large value is retained as printed (T:p3-b0, I:p3-b0). P_MW = 1.00 is the probability of originating in the Milky Way disc, not a bound probability, so it is not mapped to bound_probability. No individual distance, parallax, proper-motion, galactocentric-radius, or bound-probability values are reported for this target.

Gaia DR2 4593398670455374592: Target is the third data row of Table 1 (T:p3-b0; I:p3-b0). Table 1's P_MW=0.55 is defined in T:p3-b1 as the probability of originating in the Milky Way disc, not as a bound probability, so it is not recorded under bound_probability. No distance, parallax, or proper-motion values are reported for this star in the supplied material.

Gaia DR2 4248140165233284352: Table 1 note T:p3-b1 defines P_MW as the probability of the star originating in the Milky Way disc, not as a bound probability, so P_MW = 0.50 was not recorded as bound_probability. No parallax, distance, proper-motion, or Galactocentric radius values for this star are reported in the supplied material.

Gaia DR2 2233912206910720000: At T:p3-b1, Table 1's P_MW = 0.42 is explicitly the probability of the star originating in the Milky Way disc, not a bound probability, so it was not recorded as bound_probability. The supplied material does not report distance, parallax, proper motions, or Galactocentric radius for this star.

Gaia DR2 1268023196461923712: Target is Gaia DR2 1268023196461923712, one of the four extreme-velocity candidates serendipitously found in large spectroscopic surveys (APOGEE and LAMOST; T:p4-b1, T:p3-b7, T:p5-b11). No parallax or distance is reported for this star in the paper, so distance cannot be extracted. The P_MW = 0.49 value in Table 2 is the probability of the star originating in the Milky Way disc, not a bound probability, so it is not reported as bound_probability. V_tot and P_ub are adopted from Marchetti et al. (2018) (T:p3-b1 notes). The survey RV is from APOGEE, with the LAMOST value consistent within a few km/s (footnote a of Table 2).

Gaia DR2 6639557580310606976: For Gaia DR2 6639557580310606976, Table 2 lists RA, DEC, RV_Gaia, RV_survey, V_tot, P_MW, and P_ub. P_MW = 0.38 is defined in the Table 1/2 notes as the probability of originating in the Milky Way disc, not a bound probability, so it is not recorded as bound_probability. No distance, parallax, proper-motion, or galactocentric-radius values are reported for this star.

Gaia DR2 5212817273334550016: Target Gaia DR2 5212817273334550016 appears in Table 2 as one of four extreme-velocity candidates serendipitously observed by RAVE. The tabulated P_MW = 0.35 is the probability of the star originating in the Milky Way disc (per the Table 1 note and column definition), not a bound probability, so it is not recorded as bound_probability. The paper also reports RAVE stellar parameters for this star ([Fe/H] = -1.80 ± 0.14 dex), but these are not requested quantities. No distance or parallax is reported for this star in the supplied material.

Gaia DR2 4916199478888664320: Table 2 also lists P_MW = 0.44, but the Table 1 note defines P_MW as the probability that the star originated in the Milky Way disc, not as a bound probability; no separate bound probability is reported (T:p3-b1, T:p4-b1). No distance, parallax, proper motion, or Galactocentric radius is reported for Gaia DR2 4916199478888664320.
